newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 15.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:
* General Motors' first quarter earnings more than doubled, beating analysts' expectations. The North American division posted its strongest profit in a decade.
* USA Waste Services said it would acquire United Waste Systems in a $1.5 billion stock swap.
* The Dow Industrials closed up around 60 points as the market recovered some from its recent slide.

* Intel reported higher-than-expected first quarter earnings but said it expected sales to be flat to only slightly higher in the second quarter. The company's results drew a mixed reaction on Wall Street as some analysts expressed concern the company benefited from some extraordinary gains in the first quarter.
* Several big banks including NationsBank and First Chicago NBD posted higher quarterly profits, led more by service charges and other fees rather than lending income.
* Coca-Cola's first quarter earnings jumped 38 percent, helped by growth in its domestic soft drink volume.
* British drugs company Zeneca said the founder of its Salick Health Care unit resigned and it was assuming management of the unit's 11 cancer centers at U.S. hospitals.
* Travelers Group reported a 23 percent rise in first quarter net income, ahead of forecasts.
* Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette earnings increased 32.7 percent in the first quarter, boosted by growth in fees from mergers and acquisitions and in underwriting.
* German life insurance companies tried to distance themselves from a lawsuit seeking up to $1 billion in compensation for prewar policies confiscated from Jews.
* The Treasury market was relatively flat with the 30-year bond yield rising to 7.17 percent from 7.16.

* Michael Milken, who pioneered the use of junk bonds, agreed to extend his probation another six months so the government could finish investigating whether he honoured an agreement that barred him from the securities industry for life.
* Netscape Communication plans to incorporate a technology, which "pushes" information out to readers over the Internet, into its latest Internet browser version.
* Proposals to simplify the U.S. income tax process are inevitable around April 15.
* Xerox has a strategy to let the market drive the company during the shift from analog to digital technology.
